summary: Recorded founding vision for righthand cli as a new Entity page: an always-available CLI that a main coding LLM hands non-coding chores (admin, CI/CD, logging, docs, task tracking) to. Project is greenfield; tech stack, interface, and distribution model are open questions being scoped in the PRD interview. No code written yet. Fixed two self-introduced broken-wikilink warnings (overview is a top-level concept, not linkable from pages/).

Captured the foundational righthand invocation model from the Phase-1 PRD brainstorm: the main LLM shells out to righthand as a subprocess per task and the process is torn down when finished — stateless, not a daemon. Recorded as decision decisions/stateless-subprocess-invocation.md (with alternatives + the key consequence that all cross-task state must persist to disk/DB). Updated the righthand-cli entity: transport is now defined (subprocess via terminal), lifecycle marked stateless-per-task, linked to the decision. Fixed OKF conformance: added YAML frontmatter to architecture/file-tree.md (E1) and set its type to Artifact (E3); renamed the decision file to a clean stable slug and updated index + entity wikilinks.

Updated the righthand-cli entity page to record that it is a standalone, third-party-distributable product (own repo, installable by others), resolving the previously-open "distribution model" question. Folded in the design implication that onboarding, config discovery, and "works in anyone's repo" are now first-class concerns; demoted remaining distribution question to just the packaging/install mechanism (npm/brew/releases/etc.).

Recorded two foundational architecture decisions from the Phase-2 PRD Q3 answer and updated the righthand-cli entity to reflect them. (1) Runtime chosen as Node + TypeScript — chosen for fast startup; under the stateless subprocess-per-task model cold-start is paid every invocation, so plugin loading must stay lazy. (2) Extensible modular plugin system raised to a first-class architectural pillar — third parties author/register their own tasks/commands; this shapes the command interface, discovery, and the downstream spec. Entity's "Tech stack: undecided" and open-question #2 (language/runtime) are now resolved; new open questions added for plugin discovery/registration/author-contract. Also converted the entity's raw relative link to stateless-subprocess-invocation into a proper [[wikilink]].

Recorded the research evidence base produced this turn for righthand's problem statement. Added a Learning capturing the 5 cited failure modes of coding agents doing operational tasks (P1 hallucinated cmds, P2 context bloat, P3 token cost, P4 flow interruption, P5 session inconsistency) plus the empty-quadrant positioning. Added a reusable Rule ("Compress, don't relay" — every command returns a bounded schema'd summary, full output opt-in). Added an Artifact page pointing to the research_report.md / findings_*.md deliverables in research_righthand_problem/. Cross-linked to existing righthand-cli entity and the three existing decisions. No new code/UI this turn.

Added Concept page for "self-recursive self-building agent" (Pillar 5 / Model A — persistent LLM-generated plugin code). This was previously referenced via [[self-recursive-self-building-agent]] wikilink from the accepted llm-augmented-commands decision but had no defining page. Page documents: what it is (LLM writes + saves + registers command code), why it matters (tool adapts its own surface), key properties (persistent/first-class output, trust boundary, two open design questions: approval flow + plugin location), and relationships to the LLM-augmented + plugin-system decisions and righthand-cli. Turn was a mid-interview planning step with no finalized decision, so no decision/rule/learning was recorded.

what: Recorded two new architectural pillars and one persona decision from the PRD interview, and refreshed the central righthand-cli entity.
why: These are high-stakes architecture/scoping directions a future session needs to resume without re-deriving — especially the self-builder, whose mechanism (A/B/C) and safety stance are deliberately left open pending the user's Q5b answer.
summary: Captured three PRD-interview architecture outcomes from this turn. (1) New accepted decision "LLM-augmented commands as a first-class pillar" (Pillar 4): righthand gets its own LLM config and can invoke an LLM mid-task; commands split into "do the ops" vs "do the ops and reason about it," degrading to pure-ops when unconfigured. (2) New PROPOSED decision "Self-recursive self-building agent" (Pillar 5): the LLM can grow righthand's own command surface; mechanism is OPEN — Models A (persistent generation) / B (ad-hoc) / C (hybrid) plus approval-stance and code-location sub-questions are recorded as pending the Q5b answer. (3) New accepted decision "General-purpose persona targeting": all four personas matter, pro-dev-with-real-ops is the sharpest design target. Updated the righthand-cli entity to add Pillars 4 & 5 and the persona line, and converted its cross-links to raw [[wikilinks]] to clear W4 broken-link warnings. Also deleted an auto-generated concept page (pages/concepts/self-recursive-self-building-agent.md) that falsely asserted Model A was chosen — the turn left Q5b unanswered, so the proposed decision (not the concept stub) is authoritative.

Updated the self-recursive-self-building-agent decision (and the righthand-cli entity) to reflect the Q5c answers: the two open safety-rail sub-questions are now RESOLVED — (1) approval stance = show-and-confirm-before-install (auto-run rejected), aligning the persistent path toward Model C; (2) code location = both project-local and user-global, picked per-generation. Decision status moved from "fully pending" to "partially resolved" (generation model A/B/C still open). Cleared stale "pending Q5b / unresolved" wording in both files.

Recorded new decision D6: web research / search as a righthand capability. Captures the two flavors (shallow web-research, deep websearch-deep), the Phase-2 dependency on Pillar 4 (LLM-augmented commands), the open search-backend question (SearXNG/DuckDuckGo/Brave/Tavily/Serper), and how it reinforces the "keep noisy work out of the main LLM window" thesis. Deduped against existing decisions (P1–P5 pillars + persona/runtime/plugin decisions) — no prior research/web-search concept existed.

Added a new Concept page documenting C-AUTHOR (Command authoring and scaffolding): the explicit, first-class, human-facing path to author and scaffold new righthand commands — the contract that Pillar 3 (plugin system) needs and that Pillar 5 (self-builder) generates against. Captured its placement as foundational/MVP, the manifest-fragment schema (name/description/inputSchema/handler), the scaffolder, and the shared-contract relationship between human and LLM authoring. Note: the broader MVP-vs-Phase-2 scope cut proposed this turn was NOT recorded as a decision — it is an unconfirmed proposal the assistant is actively asking the user to confirm; it will be captured once the user answers.

Recorded two PRD-scoping outcomes from the "build all" planning turn: (1) a DECISION locking full-vision-as-v1 scope — phasing is reframed as a build sequence (dependency order), not a scope cut; nothing is feature-gated out. (2) a new CAPABILITY concept page C-RESET (factory reset), capturing the "righthand can do anything, but you can always undo it" philosophy + proposed graduated/dry-run/undo-manifest design (mechanism pending user confirmation); especially load-bearing given the self-builder writes code into righthand. Renamed the decision file to a short stable id (build-all-is-v1-scope.md) to avoid a W2 long-filename warning.

Recorded the C-RESET rollback & reset capability as a Decision (status: proposed). User clarified "reset codebase" = rollback from last changes (not a factory nuke), so rollback is primary/factory-reset secondary. Scope + safety guarantees (app code preserved, journaled-before-apply, --dry-run) are locked; the git-semantics / internal version store implementation mechanism is the assistant's recommendation, not yet user-confirmed. Cross-links [[righthand-cli]] and [[self-recursive-self-building-agent]] (rollback is the safety net that justifies the self-builder).

Recorded the LOCKED success-criteria decision (PRD Topic 4): experiential signals, a 6-row measurable-metrics table (each tagged to research pain P1–P5 / C-RESET), and 6 never-break non-functional bars. Cross-linked to stateless invocation, compress-don't-relay, self-builder, and factory-reset concepts. Noted aggressive targets (≤200ms cold-start, ≤20% token output) as architectural constraints. Did NOT record Topic 5 capability map (C1–C9) — it was presented for confirmation, not locked.

Recorded two decisions from PRD Topic 6 (Technical Approach). (1) C10 — `righthand doctor`: a config/integration diagnostics capability (checks LLM provider, search backend, CI tokens, plugin health, version) explicitly added to scope by the user this turn; status proposed. (2) Technical approach — proposed architecture: the assistant's full layer-by-layer proposed stack (hand-roll/citty CLI dispatch, shell-out-to-CLIs ops backend, internal-git state+rollback, layered config, OS-keychain credentials, npm-primary distribution, OpenAI-compatible+Anthropic LLM provider abstraction, pluggable search backend) with rationale, cross-refs to existing ADRs, and the 4 unresolved user-confirmation calls clearly marked; status proposed. Skipped C8 (five command groups) — not enumerated in this turn's text; skipped the ops "compress --json" point as already covered by the existing compress-don't-relay rule.

Recorded the decision to lock citty (UnJS) as righthand-cli's CLI framework, resolving the previously-open "hand-roll vs citty" option from the technical-approach decision. Captures alternatives considered (commander, yargs, clipanion, hand-roll) and rationale (TS-native typing, tiny dep, function-based plugin fit).

Captured 3 architecture decisions + 1 learning from the Topic-6 (Technical Approach) PRD answers: (1) PROPOSED decision to use citty over crust.js as the CLI framework, with the full citty-vs-crust comparison research preserved so it isn't redone later — crust.js is documented as the alpha-stage alternative with a real upside (Bun-native + compile-time validation); (2) accepted decision that Bun support is a hard constraint, runtime stays Node-compatible (runtime-agnostic JS), and distribution is npm-only with Bun-binary compilation deferred to Phase-2 (58–109MB binary penalty); (3) accepted decision revising the D6 search-backend open question to LLM-driven research riding the configured LLM's own web features, no hard-coupled search API in core (a search-API plugin stays optional/additive); (4) learning recording the non-obvious Bun --compile binary size and crust.js alpha maturity for future sessions. Together these resolve open questions #1 (proposed), #2, and #4 from decisions/technical-approach-proposed-architecture; the ops "wrap CLIs" answer (#3) confirmed the existing proposal and added no new info so was not recorded.

user: You can scaffold a new righthand command with `righthand new <name>` — it writes a working, auto-discoverable starter file into the footprint, journaled so it's rollback-able.
what: Implemented C3 — `righthand new` authoring & scaffolder. Generates a strip-only TS starter command (descriptor + run) into `./.righthand/commands/` or `~/.righthand/commands/`, wrapped in a journaled mutation. Honors `--scope`, `--desc`, `--dry-run`, `--force`; validates kebab-case names.
why: C3 is the explicit, first-class authoring path and the load-bearing contract the self-builder (C5) later generates against. Foundational to the plugin ecosystem — the authoring story is a command, not a buried doc.
next: Wire a generated command into `src/commands/` (or a future footprint-commands discovery path) to make it dispatchable; see docs/wiki/pages/concepts/command-authoring-and-scaffolding.
summary: Added src/scaffold.ts (renderCommand + validateName), src/commands/new.ts (mutating, journaled via journal(), sets meta.change_id, honors --dry-run/--force/--scope), and test/scaffold.test.ts (8 tests: strip-only dynamic-import smoke, dry-run no-write, journaled write + change recorded, user scope, overwrite refusal, --force overwrite, invalid name). Generated template uses only `import type` so it imports cleanly from anywhere. npm test: 68 pass (was 60, +8). `new` is auto-discovered (tools count 13→14).

user: righthand can now call an LLM: `righthand llm ask "<prompt>"` talks to any OpenAI-compatible or Anthropic provider and returns a bounded envelope.
what: Implemented C4 — LLM Provider Integration: new `src/llm.ts` (provider-agnostic `complete()` API), auto-discovered `llm` command (`src/commands/llm.ts`), and `test/llm.test.ts` (21 tests, no network).
why: C4 is the reasoning foundation that unblocks C5 (self-builder), C6 (research), and the LLM-assisted ops domains — every reasoning capability routes through `complete()`.
next: Build C6 (web research) or an LLM-assisted ops domain on top of `complete()`; add OS keychain support to `resolveApiKey` when a native dep is acceptable.
summary: Added src/llm.ts exporting LlmMessage/LlmRequest/LlmResponse + resolveProvider/resolveApiKey/complete() (OpenAI-compatible POST /chat/completions w/ Bearer; Anthropic POST /v1/messages w/ x-api-key+anthropic-version, system extracted, max_tokens floored to 1024). complete() resolves provider+key from config (opts.config ?? loadConfig()), throws CommandError(EXIT.AUTH) when no key, injects opts.fetchFn as a test seam. Added src/commands/llm.ts (descriptor capabilities=["net:llm"], costTier="cheap"; run() calls complete(), returns envelope {text,model,tokensUsed} + meta.tokens_used; no provider→AUTH(4)+needs_human; cli with positional prompt + provider flag). Added test/llm.test.ts: resolveProvider defaults/throw, resolveApiKey env:/plaintext/keychain, complete() success+auth+anthropic-header via injected fake fetch, plus 3 dispatch-level tests (capability denial, AUTH when no provider, success envelope). Suite: 68→89 righthand tests, all green (2 pre-existing failures in ops.test.ts/shell.test.ts are from parallel work, reproduce without this change). tsc clean for all 3 files.

user: Coding agents can now hand off CI/logs/docs/tasks/admin ops to righthand and get a compressed answer back
what: Added the five C8 ops command groups (ci, logs, docs, tasks, admin), a shared subprocess helper (src/shell.ts) with a runner test seam, and tests — all auto-discovered, each wrapping an existing CLI and compressing its output into the standard envelope.
why: Delivers righthand's core "compress, don't relay" value: the agent runs `righthand ci status` etc. and gets a small schema'd summary instead of ingesting a raw gh/kubectl log dump into its context. Missing wrapped binaries degrade gracefully to exit 5 (DEP_MISSING) with a needs_human hint.
next: See docs/wiki/pages/concepts/ops-domain-commands-c8.md for the group-by-group surface and docs/wiki/learnings/ops-commands-declaring-capabilities-are-capability-gated-bef.md for the capability-vs-missing-binary exit-code split.
summary: Implemented C8 (Phase-3 ops domains). New: src/shell.ts (runCli + hasBinary + setRunnerForTest seam; ENOENT→missing:true), src/commands/{ci,logs,docs,tasks,admin}.ts (each: descriptor w/ capabilities + costTier=free, run, cli; missing-binary throws CommandError(DEP_MISSING)→exit 5), test/shell.test.ts (6), test/ops.test.ts (14). Suite: 109 pass / 0 fail. Cold-start `righthand tools` 109ms (<200ms bar). Did NOT edit cli.ts/contracts.ts/runtime.ts/discover.ts/manifest.ts. Tests inject fake runners via the seam so no gh/kubectl needed.

user: Plugins can now be installed, listed, and removed from a footprint (C2).
what: Added the `righthand plugins install|list|remove` command and a plugininstall module that npm-installs packages into the footprint plugins dir, reads their manifest.json fragment, and records them in config.plugins.
why: This is the user-facing half of the plugin extensibility pillar — without install/list/remove there is nothing to consume the discovery + authoring contracts. It also establishes the test seam for subprocess npm calls (mirroring shell.ts).
next: See docs/wiki/pages/entities/plugins-command.md for the interface and test seam.
summary: Implemented C2 plugin lifecycle. New files: src/plugininstall.ts (npm runner seam — defaultNpmRunner/setNpmRunnerForTest/activeNpmRunner mirroring src/shell.ts; installPlugin/uninstallPlugin via `npm install/uninstall --prefix <pluginsDir>`; listPlugins merges config.plugins + disk scan of node_modules incl. @scope layout; readManifest/packageNameFromSpec), src/commands/plugins.ts (command: two positionals action+pkg, cli.scope:true, mutates:true; install/remove journal npm+config in one change, honor --dry-run + confirm; missing manifest registers name + warns), test/plugins.test.ts (11 tests via injected fake npm runner over isolated temp footprints). All mutating ops own their journaling per the mutating-commands decision. No edits to cli.ts/contracts.ts/discover.ts/manifest.ts/runtime.ts — plugins.ts is auto-discovered. Full suite: 120 tests pass.

Recorded the build's reusable knowledge from the autonomous righthand v1 build: (1) rule on foundation-first / fan-out-leaf parallel orchestration (the method that kept 8 agents collision-free), (2) learning that parallel workers against one repo report unreliable test snapshots (always re-run the true integrated suite), (3) new Concept page "Self-extending safe-undo loop" documenting righthand's signature story (new/build → auto-discovered → run → journaled → rollback → gone), which ties together auto-discovery, journaling, and the rollback store. Fixed a truncated cross-link slug in the rule.

user: `righthand build` with no provider now signals AUTH (exit 4) instead of a vague "needs human"
what: `build --yes` wrapped *all* LLM-call failures — including missing-provider AUTH — as `needs_human` (exit 3), inconsistent with `righthand llm ask` (exit 4). Structured `CommandError` (AUTH/DEP_MISSING) now propagates to dispatch so the precise exit code surfaces; only unexpected failures wrap as exit 3.
why: Exit 4 (auth/credential) tells the caller exactly what to fix; exit 3 (needs human) is a generic escalation. Consistent exit codes across `llm` and `build` mean callers can branch reliably.

summary: Recorded learning: .env auto-loading + generalized env: indirection to baseURL/model. Updated llm-provider-integration entity page: added resolveEnvRef() to the documented interface contract and a .env-loading note under Configuration. No E1-E3 errors introduced.
